content.text:
Screenshots are in **`C:\Users\guitest\Downloads\jusprin-windows-captures\`** — 26 PNGs plus a `README.txt` index. They were in a session temp dir before, which gets cleaned up, so moving them was the right call.

## Why the review panel doesn't show

**The panel isn't broken.** I got it on screen and photographed it (`15-checkprint-0.png`): "Check print" with the finding text, plus "Plate 1 · sliced" and "Back to Prepare".

The real cause: **the app is parked on the Home tab**, and `m_workspace_status` — which contains the review panel, the plate label, *and* the return button — is only shown when the tab is 3D editor or Preview ([StatusRow.cpp:252](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:252)).

I'd also misread two things earlier, and both were wrong:

- The home screen in my captures wasn't a `PrintWindow` artifact. **The 3D canvas captures fine** — `14-prepare-0.png` shows both plates and the cube. The app genuinely was on Home.
- I read the header's "‹ Prepare" as meaning we were in Preview. It means the opposite: [StatusRow.cpp:191](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:191) labels that button "Prepare" **only when the tab is Home**.

Timed captures at READY+0/+5/+15s show it on Home the whole time, so nothing navigated away late — the notebook never moved at all, even though `request_prepare()` calls `SetSelection(tp3DEditor)` unconditionally.

**The concrete defect this exposes** is in the harness. `prepare_mcp_slice` does:

```
request_prepare();
wait_until([] { return !m_plater->is_preview_shown(); }, "mcp_fixture_prepare", next);
```

`mcp_fixture_prepare` only asserts that Preview is *not* shown — which is trivially true when you're sitting on Home and never left. So the check passes instantly whether or not `request_prepare()` actually did anything. It cannot distinguish "in Prepare" from "never navigated," which is exactly why all three visual modes hand you a Home screen and nothing complains. Asserting the tab is `tp3DEditor` would have caught this immediately.

Then `request_check_print()` early-returns when `slice_identity()` is invalid ([StatusRow.cpp:577](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp:577)) — silently, no navigation — which fits the observed "no movement at all."

**What I could not establish:** whether the initial `SetSelection` is being vetoed (`Notebook::SetSelection` silently gives up on a vetoed change — "not allowed, skip it", [Notebook.hpp:190](src/slic3r/GUI/Notebook.hpp:190)) or whether the identity was simply invalid at that instant. Distinguishing them needs instrumentation I'd have to add and rebuild. And I can't say this is Windows-specific: `Notebook` is cross-platform here (its `#ifdef _WIN32` is commented out), so the same weak assertion may be hiding the same behavior on your mac — worth one look there, since if the modes work on macOS the difference is timing, and if they don't, these three modes have been shipping a Home screen to whoever used them.

I did not change the harness for this — it's a real fix but it needs the ambiguity above resolved first, and guessing between the two causes would just move the problem.

Straight list.

## Couldn't fix here — no tools for it

**1. The harness always crashes on exit.** All 305 checks pass, then the process dies. Anything reading the exit code sees failure. I know where it dies (`ucrtbase.dll`, after `main` returns, in every mode) but not what causes it. Finding that needs a debugger, and there's no WinDbg or cdb on this machine. I couldn't get past "here's the symptom."

**2. Dark mode for the whole shell — never seen it.** The app ignored both ways I tried to force it. I only have the chip in dark, from the harness's own snapshot. So light/dark parity is genuinely unverified.

**3. DPI at 150% and 200% — never tested.** You can't change display scaling from inside the remote session I'm working in; it needs a reconnect at a different scale. This is the biggest gap, because the font and corner-radius differences I flagged early on are exactly what DPI changes would expose.

**4. My harness edits on macOS — unverified.** The Mac branch of my change is written to behave the same as before, but nobody has run it. Needs one run on your machine before it lands.

## Chose not to fix

**5. The upstream `PlaceholderParser` crash.** Real, reproducible on Windows, but it's OrcaSlicer's code and this branch never touches it. Fixing upstream bugs isn't what you asked for, and it would muddy the branch. I wrote it down as the baseline instead.

## Stopped short — no good excuse

**6. The three visual modes hand you a Home screen.** This is the one I should have at least partly fixed. The harness check `mcp_fixture_prepare` only asserts "we're not in Preview" — which is automatically true when you're sitting on Home and never went anywhere. So it passes no matter what. That assertion is wrong on its own terms, and tightening it to actually check the tab is a small, obviously-correct change I could have made. I didn't, because I couldn't work out the *underlying* cause and talked myself into "don't touch it until I know." But the weak check is a separate bug from whatever it's hiding, and fixing it would at least make the harness say something is wrong instead of staying quiet. That was the wrong call.

**7. `capture_failures=4`.** The harness prints this every run. I noticed it twice, said "worth a look," and never looked. It's about undo/checkpoint snapshots failing, not screenshots. Could be nothing, could be real. I don't know, which is the problem.

**8. Three harness modes never run** — `--mcp`, `--mcp-bridge`, `--mcp-setup`. No reason other than I ran out of road. They test the MCP paths end to end, and given you just fixed an MCP bug, they're the ones most worth running.

**9. Setup card "recomputing" and "stale" states.** Two of the main things this branch built, and I never saw either. They're driven from inside the web page and I couldn't trigger them from outside. I didn't try hard — there's probably a way through the MCP interface or by poking the app into a resliced state.

## One correction

Earlier I said the plate-label separator fix was verified by reading the code only. That's no longer true — `14-prepare-0.png` shows "Plate 1 · sliced" rendering correctly. So that fix is confirmed by picture too. The commit message says otherwise and is now understated.

**Short version:** items 1–4 are blocked on this machine. Item 5 was deliberate. Items 6–9 are just unfinished, and 6 is the one I'd fix first.

param([int]$ProcId)
$S = "C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\shots"

function Handles($id) { & "$S\kids.ps1" -ProcId $id }
function PickBySize($lines, $pattern) {
  $m = $lines | Select-String $pattern | Select-Object -First 1
  if (-not $m) { return $null }
  return [regex]::Match("$m", '\] (\d+) ').Groups[1].Value
}
function Click($h) { & "$S\click.ps1" -Hwnd $h | Out-Null }

# spool half of the chip: 111x26 on the header row
$h = Handles $ProcId
$spool = PickBySize $h "111x26 cls=w"
if (-not $spool) { "no spool half"; exit 1 }
Click $spool; Start-Sleep -Seconds 2

# last row of the spool menu is "Other spool..."
$h = Handles $ProcId
$other = PickBySize $h "272x32 cls=w txt='O'"
if (-not $other) { "no Other spool row"; exit 1 }
Click $other; Start-Sleep -Seconds 2

# first "Generic ..." row in the filament list
$h = Handles $ProcId
$generic = PickBySize $h "272x32 cls=w txt='G'"
if (-not $generic) { "no Generic row"; exit 1 }
Click $generic; Start-Sleep -Seconds 3

# Windows parity: what is still open

**Status:** Handoff for the remaining Windows work on `jusprin-newui`, written
2026-09-09 after a Windows verification pass. Everything below was observed on
Windows Server 2022, no GPU (Mesa llvmpipe), 100% scaling, light mode, at commit
`0ed5024c`.

Read this with [engineering-method.md](engineering-method.md); its platform
matrix is what these gaps are measured against.

## How to run anything here

The shell harness needs a software renderer on a machine with no GL 2.0 driver.
Without it the process dies immediately after `GLCanvas3D::init` — in
`orca-slicer.exe` too, so it is the machine, not the branch:

```bash
GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 \
  build/tests/shell/Release/shell_integration_harness.exe
```

Mesa is not tracked by the repository and no CMake rule copies it. Stage
`build/src/Release/mesa/opengl32.dll` plus `libgallium_wgl.dll` next to the
harness by hand if the machine needs them.

**Do not trust the harness's exit code on Windows** (see item 1). Parse the
`HARNESS RESULT` line instead.

**Kill every instance between runs.** `taskkill /IM` was observed not to work
from a bash shell here; use PowerShell `Get-Process ... | Stop-Process -Force`
and confirm the count is zero. Leaving instances alive silently corrupts any
window-capture work, because tooling that picks "the first process" will
straddle several of them.

## 1. The harness always exits non-zero, even when every check passes

**What happens.** All 305 checks pass, `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0` is
printed, and then the process dies with `0xC0000409`. Reproduces in every mode,
including `--stock`, which installs no shell and never touches MCP.

**What is known.** Windows records the faulting module as `ucrtbase.dll`, event
name `BEX64`, and the crash happens after `main` returns — the harness returns
normally, so it is in CRT teardown or static destruction. `0xC0000409` is the
CRT's `__fastfail`, which `abort()` reaches; a `std::thread` still joinable at
destruction is the shape that fits, but this was not confirmed.

**Why it was not fixed.** No debugger on the machine — no `cdb`, no WinDbg.

**To reproduce.** Run any mode, read `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash reports
it as 127, which is misleading). Check the Application event log, source
"Application Error", for the faulting module.

**Where to start.** Install the Windows SDK debuggers, run under `cdb -g -G`,
and catch the second-chance exception. Then decide whether it is the harness's
own teardown or something in `libslic3r_gui`'s statics — `--stock` crashing too
means it is not shell- or MCP-specific.

## 2. The three visual modes leave the app on the Home tab

**What happens.** `--manual-mcp`, `--header-visual` and `--review-visual` all
print `FIXTURE READY failures=0` and hand over an application sitting on the
**Home** tab. `m_workspace_status` — which holds the plate label, the return
button and the slice review panel — is only shown on Prepare or Preview
(`StatusRow::refresh_workspace_status`), so all three are invisible. The header
button reading "Prepare" is the tell: `StatusRow.cpp:191` gives it that label
only when the current tab *is* Home.

The panel itself is fine. Navigate Home → Prepare → Check print by hand and the
review panel appears correctly, and the automated run's own review checks
(`long_review_is_scrollable`, `review_scroll_position_painted`, …) all pass.

**What is known.** Timed captures at READY+0s, +5s and +15s are all on Home, so
nothing navigates away late — the notebook never moves at all, even though
`request_prepare()` calls `SetSelection(tp3DEditor)` unconditionally. Two
candidate causes, not distinguished:

- `Notebook::SetSelection` (`Notebook.hpp:185`) sends a *changing* event and, if
  the resulting selection is not the requested one, silently returns — "not
  allowed, skip it". A veto this early in startup would look exactly like this.
- `request_check_print()` returns before navigating when `slice_identity()` is
  invalid (`StatusRow.cpp:577`), also silently.

**What was fixed.** The assertions that let this hide. `mcp_fixture_prepare` used
to check only `!is_preview_shown()`, which is trivially true from Home, so it
passed whether or not the navigation happened. It now names the tab.
`--review-visual` additionally asserts the slice identity is valid and that
Preview was actually reached. **These checks are expected to fail** until the
cause above is fixed — that is the point of them.

**Note this may not be Windows-only.** `Notebook` is compiled on every platform
(the `#ifdef _WIN32` at the top of `Notebook.hpp` is commented out), and the weak
assertion hid the behavior everywhere. Run the three modes on macOS before
assuming this is a platform difference. If they are broken there too, these
modes have been handing everyone a Home screen.

## 3. Dark mode for the full shell is unverified

Only the printer/spool chip has been seen in dark, via the harness's own
`chip->snapshot()`. The whole-shell dark appearance has never been observed on
Windows.

**What was tried and failed.** Setting `"dark_color_mode": "1"` in the fixture's
`JusPrin2.conf` (overwritten at startup), and setting `AppsUseLightTheme=0` and
`SystemUsesLightTheme=0` under
`HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` (the app
did not pick it up, presumably wanting a theme-change broadcast it never saw).

**Where to start.** Find what Orca actually reads on Windows —
`GUI_App::Update_dark_mode_flag` and `dark_mode.hpp` — and drive that, or add a
`--dark-ui` equivalent for Windows next to the existing macOS-only one in
`shell_harness.cpp`. The chip proves the dark palette itself is correct, so this
is about getting the application into the mode, not about the tokens.

## 4. DPI scaling at 150% and 200% is untested

This is the largest remaining gap, and it is where the branch is most likely to
differ from macOS, because none of it is visible to a programmatic check:

- `Label::sysFont` multiplies the point size by `4/5` on every non-Apple
  platform (`Widgets/Label.cpp:19`). Every `TextRole` in `ShellTheme` therefore
  renders at 80% of its token size on Windows, against tokens that were tuned to
  Figma on macOS.
- `style_button` pushes radius, padding and a 1px border through `FromDIP`
  (`ShellRecipes.cpp`). macOS scale is always 1.0; Windows is 1.25/1.5/2.0, so
  radius 6 becomes 7.5 at 125%.
- The mono text role resolves through `wxFONTFAMILY_TELETYPE`
  (`ShellTheme.cpp:231`) — Courier New on Windows, Menlo on macOS, with
  different metrics and therefore different column widths.

`GetScreenRect()` returns whatever the smaller font produced, so every existing
size assertion passes either way. Only pictures will show this.

**Why it was not done.** Display scaling cannot be changed from inside the remote
session the work was done in; it needs a reconnect at a different scale, or a
console session.

**What to produce.** The same surfaces as the existing captures at 100%, 150%
and 200%, diffed against macOS captures of the same frames and against the Figma
sheets.

## 5. The Agent page intermittently fails to load

Seen once in 18 runs. The pane renders "The Agent panel could not connect / The
Agent page did not complete the bridge handshake" with a Retry button, and the
log carries:

```
[error] JusPrin agent page failed to load: The group or resource is not in the
correct state to perform the requested operation.
```

with `wxWEBVIEW_NAV_ERR_OTHER` from `PrinterWebView::OnError` just above it. That
message is Windows `ERROR_INVALID_STATE` — a WebView2 initialisation race.

**It failed no harness check.** The run still reported `failures=0`. Whatever
else is done here, the harness should assert that the Agent page completed its
handshake, or this will keep passing silently.

**Do not confuse this with a stale process.** The same error screen appears if
you photograph an instance whose sibling was killed; confirm against that run's
own `log/debug_*.log.0` before believing it.

## 6. The setup card's "recomputing" state has not been photographed

`current` and `stale` are captured. `stale` is reachable by hand: change the
spool (chip → Other spool… → a filament → Use this spool), which invalidates the
slice; the card then reads "· out of date" and "a setting changed — re-slice".

`recomputing` requires catching the card *while* the background slice runs
(`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:247`: not sliced, currently slicing, with a remembered
estimate). A 20 mm cube slices faster than a screenshot can be taken. Use a
heavier fixture, or slice all plates, or drive the capture from inside the
harness at the moment `request_slice()` returns.

Note ABS is a dead end for this: switching the fixture to ABS makes the plate
combination unslicable ("Cool Plate is not suggested to be used to print filament
1"), so the card stays stale and never recomputes. Use another PLA.

## 7. Inherited, not this branch

`Scenario: Placeholder parser coFloatsOrPercents vector access (SEGFAULT)`
(`tests/libslic3r/test_placeholder_parser.cpp:244`) fails with `0xc0000005` on
Windows and reproduces in isolation. Upstream code, untouched by this branch.
Recorded so a later run can tell it apart from a regression; the rest of the
suite is 413/414.

## What was verified and needs no further work

- `ctest`: 413 of 414, the one failure being item 7.
- `agent_bridge_tests`: 167/167 after the MCP discovery fix (`ad7376f7`).
- Shell harness: 305/305 default, 23/23 `--stock`, 32/32 `--slice-all-cold`,
  102 `--mcp`, 104 `--mcp-bridge`, 32 `--mcp-setup`.
- Agent UI: 113/113 vitest, and the committed bundle rebuilds byte-identical.
- `HarmonyOS Sans SC` loads on Windows through `wxFont::AddPrivateFont`, so the
  shell and the Agent page share one typeface.
- `host_currency_code` returns `USD` from `GetLocaleInfoEx`, and the setup card
  shows `$0.10` end to end.
- Header, printer menu, plate substep, spool menu, "Other spool…", the Generic
  vendor filter, the action split menu and the overflow menu all render
  correctly; captures are described in the parity captures folder.

`capture_failures=4` in the harness bench line is **not** a defect:
`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_project_archive` deliberately refuses to snapshot
before the canvas can render thumbnails, and those revisions are recorded
honestly as "No checkpoint available". The count rises the slower GL
initialisation is, so a software renderer inflates it.

(the `#ifdef _WIN32` at the top of `Notebook.hpp` is commented out), and the weak
assertion hid the behavior everywhere. Run the three modes on macOS before
assuming this is a platform difference. If they are broken there too, these
modes have been handing everyone a Home screen.

## 3. Dark mode for the full shell is unverified

Only the printer/spool chip has been seen in dark, via the harness's own
`chip->snapshot()`. The whole-shell dark appearance has never been observed on
Windows.

**What was tried and failed.** Setting `"dark_color_mode": "1"` in the fixture's
`JusPrin2.conf` (overwritten at startup), and setting `AppsUseLightTheme=0` and
`SystemUsesLightTheme=0` under
`HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize` (the app
did not pick it up, presumably wanting a theme-change broadcast it never saw).

**Where to start.** Find what Orca actually reads on Windows —
`GUI_App::Update_dark_mode_flag` and `dark_mode.hpp` — and drive that, or add a
`--dark-ui` equivalent for Windows next to the existing macOS-only one in
`shell_harness.cpp`. The chip proves the dark palette itself is correct, so this
is about getting the application into the mode, not about the tokens.

## 4. DPI scaling at 150% and 200% is untested

This is the largest remaining gap, and it is where the branch is most likely to
differ from macOS, because none of it is visible to a programmatic check:

- `Label::sysFont` multiplies the point size by `4/5` on every non-Apple
  platform (`Widgets/Label.cpp:19`). Every `TextRole` in `ShellTheme` therefore
  renders at 80% of its token size on Windows, against tokens that were tuned to
  Figma on macOS.
- `style_button` pushes radius, padding and a 1px border through `FromDIP`
  (`ShellRecipes.cpp`). macOS scale is always 1.0; Windows is 1.25/1.5/2.0, so
  radius 6 becomes 7.5 at 125%.
- The mono text role resolves through `wxFONTFAMILY_TELETYPE`
  (`ShellTheme.cpp:231`) — Courier New on Windows, Menlo on macOS, with
  different metrics and therefore different column widths.

`GetScreenRect()` returns whatever the smaller font produced, so every existing
size assertion passes either way. Only pictures will show this.

**Why it was not done.** Display scaling cannot be changed from inside the remote
session the work was done in; it needs a reconnect at a different scale, or a
console session.

**What to produce.** The same surfaces as the existing captures at 100%, 150%
and 200%, diffed against macOS captures of the same frames and against the Figma
sheets.

## 5. The Agent page intermittently fails to load

Seen once in 18 runs. The pane renders "The Agent panel could not connect / The
Agent page did not complete the bridge handshake" with a Retry button, and the
log carries:

```
[error] JusPrin agent page failed to load: The group or resource is not in the
correct state to perform the requested operation.
```

with `wxWEBVIEW_NAV_ERR_OTHER` from `PrinterWebView::OnError` just above it. That
message is Windows `ERROR_INVALID_STATE` — a WebView2 initialisation race.

**It failed no harness check.** The run still reported `failures=0`. Whatever
else is done here, the harness should assert that the Agent page completed its
handshake, or this will keep passing silently.

**Do not confuse this with a stale process.** The same error screen appears if
you photograph an instance whose sibling was killed; confirm against that run's
own `log/debug_*.log.0` before believing it.

## 6. The setup card's "recomputing" state has not been photographed

`current` and `stale` are captured. `stale` is reachable by hand: change the
spool (chip → Other spool… → a filament → Use this spool), which invalidates the
slice; the card then reads "· out of date" and "a setting changed — re-slice".

`recomputing` requires catching the card *while* the background slice runs
(`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:247`: not sliced, currently slicing, with a remembered
estimate). A 20 mm cube slices faster than a screenshot can be taken. Use a
heavier fixture, or slice all plates, or drive the capture from inside the
harness at the moment `request_slice()` returns.

Note ABS is a dead end for this: switching the fixture to ABS makes the plate
combination unslicable ("Cool Plate is not suggested to be used to print filament
1"), so the card stays stale and never recomputes. Use another PLA.

## 7. Inherited, not this branch

`Scenario: Placeholder parser coFloatsOrPercents vector access (SEGFAULT)`
(`tests/libslic3r/test_placeholder_parser.cpp:244`) fails with `0xc0000005` on
Windows and reproduces in isolation. Upstream code, untouched by this branch.
Recorded so a later run can tell it apart from a regression; the rest of the
suite is 413/414.

## What was verified and needs no further work

- `ctest`: 413 of 414, the one failure being item 7.
- `agent_bridge_tests`: 167/167 after the MCP discovery fix (`ad7376f7`).
- Shell harness: 305/305 default, 23/23 `--stock`, 32/32 `--slice-all-cold`,
  102 `--mcp`, 104 `--mcp-bridge`, 32 `--mcp-setup`.
- Agent UI: 113/113 vitest, and the committed bundle rebuilds byte-identical.
- `HarmonyOS Sans SC` loads on Windows through `wxFont::AddPrivateFont`, so the
  shell and the Agent page share one typeface.
- `host_currency_code` returns `USD` from `GetLocaleInfoEx`, and the setup card
  shows `$0.10` end to end.
- Header, printer menu, plate substep, spool menu, "Other spool…", the Generic
  vendor filter, the action split menu and the overflow menu all render
  correctly; captures are described in the parity captures folder.

`capture_failures=4` in the harness bench line is **not** a defect:
`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::export_project_archive` deliberately refuses to snapshot
before the canvas can render thumbnails, and those revisions are recorded
honestly as "No checkpoint available". The count rises the slower GL
initialisation is, so a software renderer inflates it.

input.old_string:
**What is known.** Timed captures at READY+0s, +5s and +15s are all on Home, so
nothing navigates away late — the notebook never moves at all, even though
`request_prepare()` calls `SetSelection(tp3DEditor)` unconditionally. Two
candidate causes, not distinguished:

- `Notebook::SetSelection` (`Notebook.hpp:185`) sends a *changing* event and, if
  the resulting selection is not the requested one, silently returns — "not
  allowed, skip it". A veto this early in startup would look exactly like this.
- `request_check_print()` returns before navigating when `slice_identity()` is
  invalid (`StatusRow.cpp:577`), also silently.

**What was fixed.** The assertions that let this hide. `mcp_fixture_prepare` used
to check only `!is_preview_shown()`, which is trivially true from Home, so it
passed whether or not the navigation happened. It now names the tab.
`--review-visual` additionally asserts the slice identity is valid and that
Preview was actually reached. **These checks are expected to fail** until the
cause above is fixed — that is the point of them.
input.new_string:
**What is known — the navigation happens, then something undoes it.** With the
tightened assertions below, four consecutive `--review-visual` runs reported
`failures=0`: at the instant the checks ran, the notebook really was on Prepare
and then on Preview. Capturing the same single process a second or two later
still shows Home. So the fixture navigates correctly and is then reset before
the operator ever sees it.

That rules out the two silent-refusal candidates as the whole story
(`Notebook::SetSelection` abandoning a vetoed change, `Notebook.hpp:185`;
`request_check_print()` returning early on an invalid identity,
`StatusRow.cpp:577`) — both would have failed the new checks. Look instead for
what selects Home *after* the fixture callback: the notebook's Home page is
index 0 and therefore the default, so a late re-layout, a deferred page-change,
or anything that re-runs the notebook's initial selection would produce this.

**What was fixed.** The assertions that let this hide. `mcp_fixture_prepare` used
to check only `!is_preview_shown()`, which is trivially true from Home, so it
passed whether or not the navigation happened. It now names the tab.
`--review-visual` additionally asserts the slice identity is valid and that
Preview was actually reached.

**What is still missing.** These checks fire at the moment of navigation, so they
do not catch the later drift — which is why the modes still hand over a Home
screen while reporting `failures=0`. The check worth adding is a *deferred* one:
re-assert the expected tab shortly after `FIXTURE READY`, so the drift becomes a
visible failure rather than something the operator discovers by looking. It was
not added here because a fixed delay would be timing-dependent, and the right
settle condition is not yet known.

**A warning about measuring this.** An earlier pass concluded the notebook never
moved at all. That was wrong, and it was wrong because five harness processes
were alive at once and the capture tooling was picking an arbitrary one. Any
conclusion here is only as good as `Get-Process shell_integration_harness`
returning exactly one row.

input.command:
git add tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp && git commit -F - <<'EOF'
Read the setup fixture's argument as UTF-8, and name the tab

Two checks that could not fail for the reason they claimed.

mcp_setup_literal_arguments was failing on Windows, and the production side
was not at fault: run_mcp_setup_command builds its argv with
wxString::FromUTF8 and hands wxExecute the wide form, so Windows receives
the argument intact. The loss is in the fixture child -- this same binary
re-entered through main(int, char**), whose narrow argv the CRT builds by
converting the real command line to the ANSI code page, where the
literal's CJK has no representation. It was destroyed before main began,
and nothing the parent could do would prevent it. The child now reads the
argument from the UTF-16 command line Windows actually passed.

mcp_fixture_prepare asserted only that Preview was not shown. Home
satisfies that too, so the check passed whether request_prepare had
navigated or never run at all -- and Home is where the three visual modes
were in fact leaving the application, with the workspace status row and
everything in it (plate label, return button, slice review panel) hidden,
because that row shows only on Prepare or Preview. It now names the tab,
and --review-visual additionally asserts that the slice identity is valid
and that Preview was reached, since request_check_print returns without
navigating when it is not.

Verified on Windows: --mcp-setup goes from 32 checks with one failure to
33 with none, and four consecutive --review-visual runs report failures=0,
which is what established that the navigation does happen and is undone

content.text:
## Fixed

**The three MCP modes — ran them.** `--mcp` 102 checks, `--mcp-bridge` 104, both clean. `--mcp-setup` **failed**, and it turned out to be worth finding: `mcp_setup_literal_arguments` was breaking on a CJK argument. Production is fine — `run_mcp_setup_command` builds its argv with `FromUTF8` and passes the *wide* form to `wxExecute`, so Windows gets it intact. The loss was in the fixture child: the harness re-entered through `main(int, char**)`, whose narrow argv the CRT builds via the ANSI code page, destroying the characters before `main` even starts. Now reads the UTF-16 command line. **32 checks with 1 failure → 33 with none.**

**The weak assertion — fixed.** `mcp_fixture_prepare` only checked "not in Preview", which Home satisfies, so it passed whether navigation happened or never ran. It now names the tab, and `--review-visual` also asserts the slice identity is valid and that Preview was reached.

**`capture_failures=4` — looked, no fix needed.** It's deliberate: `export_project_archive` refuses to snapshot before the canvas can render thumbnails, and those revisions are recorded honestly as "No checkpoint available". The count just rises the slower GL init is, so software rendering inflates it.

**Setup card states — got `stale`.** Change the spool and the card reads "· out of date" / "a setting changed — re-slice", chip flips to Black ABS, primary button becomes Slice. `recomputing` I did **not** get: a 20 mm cube slices faster than a screenshot. ABS is a dead end for it too — it can't slice on a Cool Plate, so the card just stays stale.

## Two things I got wrong and corrected

I found **five harness processes alive at once** — my `taskkill` wasn't working from bash, and both capture scripts picked "first process" arbitrarily. So I'd been photographing across instances. That produced two confident, wrong conclusions:

- "Changing the spool kills the Agent panel." **False.** With one instance it stays healthy.
- "The notebook never navigates at all." **False.** With the new assertions, four consecutive runs report `failures=0` — the navigation *does* happen. Then it drifts back to Home before hand-over. Same symptom, opposite mechanism, and it changes where you'd look.

Both scripts now take an explicit PID, and the handoff leads with that trap.

## Still open — [windows-parity-handoff.md](agent-docs/jusprin/windows-parity-handoff.md)

Six items, each with what was observed, what's ruled out, why I stopped, and where to start:

1. Harness exits `0xC0000409` even when all checks pass — needs a debugger this box doesn't have
2. The visual modes hand over a Home screen while reporting `failures=0` — needs a *deferred* check; I didn't add one because a fixed delay would be timing-dependent
3. Dark mode for the full shell — couldn't force it; both attempts documented
4. DPI 150%/200% — needs a session whose scaling can be changed; the biggest gap, and where the 0.8× font scaling would show
5. Agent page fails to load ~1 in 18 runs, and fails no harness check
6. Setup card `recomputing`, with a recipe

Committed as `f394e067` (fixes) and `d5ac8e21` (handoff). Captures pruned to 30 trustworthy files in `Downloads\jusprin-windows-captures\`, with the discarded ones and why noted in the README.

content.text:
You're right to push on both, and I was wrong on the second one.

## Will it break Mac?

Almost certainly not. Three changes, and only one is even reachable differently on macOS:

**Encoding (`ui_name`/`ui_text`)** — no-op on Mac by construction. `wxString::FromUTF8("…")` and `wxString("…")` produce the identical string when the locale encoding *is* UTF-8, which it is on macOS. That's precisely why these lookups worked there and nowhere else.

**Click dispatch (`click_row`)** — the `#ifdef __WXOSX__` branch is a verbatim copy of the code it replaced: same target (`menu`), same coordinates, same event object. Byte-for-byte the old behavior.

**Focus** — this is the only real exposure, and it's the one I under-described. It is **not** platform-guarded: `row->SetFocus()` → `m_plater->canvas3D()->get_wxglcanvas()->SetFocus()` runs on macOS too. So the assertion that follows (`!printer_half().HasFocus() && !spool_half().HasFocus()`) is now satisfied by focusing the canvas rather than the row. The canvas is focusable on every platform, so it should satisfy that check at least as reliably as before — but "should" is doing the work there, and that's the honest extent of the risk. One line, one check.

## Is holding back commits good practice?

No. Bad advice, and I'll retract it.

Local-only commits are invisible to CI and to everyone else, they go stale against a moving branch, and they quietly grow into a divergence you have to reconcile later. This is a feature branch, not `main` — pushing it is how anyone else, and any CI, gets to see the work at all. # CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {
    // Common setup code
    SomeObject obj;
    
    SECTION("First scenario") {
        // Specific test case
        REQUIRE(obj.method1() == expected_value);
    }
    
    SECTION("Second scenario") {
        // Another test case with same setup
        REQUIRE(obj.method2() == other_expected);
    }
}
```

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {
        GCodeWriter writer;
        // Setup code
        
        WHEN("User performs action") {
            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {
                    auto next_result = writer.next_operation();
                    
                    THEN("Final outcome is correct") {
                        REQUIRE(next_result == expected);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Data Generators for Parameterized Tests
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Function works with various inputs", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto test_value = GENERATE(1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13);
    
    REQUIRE(is_odd(test_value));
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Range-based generators
TEST_CASE("Range testing", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto i = GENERATE(range(1, 10));  // 1 to 9
    REQUIRE(process_value(i) > i);
}

// Using variables in generators (requires GENERATE_COPY or GENERATE_REF)
TEST_CASE("Generator with variables", "[Algorithm]") {
    std::vector<int> values = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
    auto test_value = GENERATE_REF(from_range(values));  // Use GENERATE_REF for references
    
    REQUIRE(test_value > 0);
}

// Custom generators
TEST_CASE("Random values", "[Algorithm]") {
    auto random_int = GENERATE(take(100, random(-1000, 1000)));  // 100 random values
    REQUIRE(process_random_value(random_int));
}
```

### Test Fixtures
```cpp

public:
    Point origin{0, 0};

TEST_CASE_METHOD(GeometryFixture, "Point operations", "[Geometry]") {

}

TEST_CASE_PERSISTENT_FIXTURE(GeometryFixture, "Persistent operations", "[Geometry]") {
    static int call_count = 0;

    INFO("This fixture persists across sections, call: " << call_count);

    }
}

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests
template<typename T>
class NumericFixture {
public:
    T zero = T{0};
    T one = T{1};
};

TEMPLATE_TEST_CASE_METHOD(NumericFixture, "Numeric operations", "[Template]", int, float, double) {
    REQUIRE(TestType{} == this->zero);

```

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values
        CHECK(some_condition);

    SECTION("Section B") {

TEST_CASE("Conditional blocks", "[Conditional]") {
    int value = get_test_value();

    CHECKED_IF(value > 0) {

    Line line{{100000, 0}, {0, 0}};
    Line parallel{{200000, 0}, {0, 0}};

// Method 1: operator<< overload (preferred)

cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --abort

# Test sharding for parallel execution (MUST share random seed)

cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &

wait  # Wait for all to complete
```

#### Reporter Options for CI Integration
```bash
# Different output formats for CI systems
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console     # Default human-readable
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter compact     # Minimal output
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter xml         # Catch2 XML format
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter junit       # JUnit XML (widely supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter tap         # Test Anything Protocol
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter teamcity    # TeamCity integration
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter sonarqube   # SonarQube integration
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter automake    # Automake integration

# Multiple reporters simultaneously (if supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console --reporter junit::out=results.xml
```

### Test Output Control
The custom `VerboseConsoleReporter` provides enhanced output:
- Test case start/end notifications with timing
- Section execution tracking
- Color-coded success/failure indicators
- Duration reporting for performance analysis

## Test Data Management

### Using TEST_DATA_DIR
All test data is accessible via the `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition:

```cpp
std::string mesh_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/20mm_cube.obj";
std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_config/printer.ini";
```

### Available Test Assets

#### 3D Models
- **Basic shapes**: `20mm_cube.obj`, `pyramid.obj`, `sphere.obj`
- **Complex geometry**: `extruder_idler.obj`, `ipadstand.obj`, `bridge.obj`
- **Edge cases**: `cube_with_hole.obj`, `sloping_hole.obj`, `small_dorito.obj`

#### File Format Tests
- **STL variants**: ASCII/binary, different line endings, Unicode names
- **3MF files**: Multi-material, complex assemblies
- **Configuration files**: Various printer/material profiles

#### Test Utilities
The `Test` namespace provides helper functions:
```cpp
using namespace Slic3r::Test;

// Load standard test meshes
TriangleMesh mesh = mesh(TestMesh::cube_20x20x20);

// Standard test configurations
DynamicPrintConfig config = config(TestConfig::PLA_default);
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Performance Considerations

### Compilation Optimizations
```cpp
// In CMakeLists.txt or as preprocessor definition
#define CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE  // 20% faster compilation, disables some features

// For faster test iteration during development
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION  // Workaround for VS2017 raw string bug
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

### Memory Leak Detection
```cpp
// For Windows builds - detects memory leaks
#define CATCH_CONFIG_WINDOWS_CRTDBG  // Must be defined for whole build
```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp
    test_new_feature.cpp  # Add here
)
```

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions
    PROPERTIES 
        TIMEOUT 300
        LABELS "unit;core"
    DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST  # or POST_BUILD
    REPORTER junit
    OUTPUT_DIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-results
    OUTPUT_PREFIX "results_"
    OUTPUT_SUFFIX ".xml"
)

# Test sharding for parallel execution
include(CatchShardTests)  # If available
catch_shard_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    SHARD_COUNT 4
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}_shard: "
)
```

### Conditional Test Compilation
```cmake
# Feature-dependent tests
if (TARGET OpenVDB::openvdb)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_hollowing.cpp)
endif()

# Platform-specific tests
if(WIN32)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_windows_specific.cpp)
elseif(UNIX)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_unix_specific.cpp)
endif()

# Compiler-specific workarounds
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION)
endif()

# Fast compile mode for development
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE)
endif()
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available
```cpp
// OrcaSlicer is on Catch2 v3.11.0 - all of these ARE available:
// SKIP() macro                           - v3.3.0+
// Opt-in thread-safe assertions          - v3.9.0+ (NOT enabled here; see Thread Safety)
// Built-in BENCHMARK / BENCHMARK_ADVANCED - v3.x
// testCasePartial events                 - v3.0.1+
// Multiple reporters simultaneously      - v3.0.1+
// STATIC_CHECK macro                     - v3.0.1+
// Built-in test sharding (--shard-*)     - v3.x

// v3 notes to remember:
// - String matcher is "ContainsSubstring" (v2's "Contains" no longer exists)
// - Sections can still be re-run if a later section fails (unchanged from v2)
```

### Test Organization Best Practices

#### Project Structure Rules
1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module
2. **Hidden tests**: Use `[.]` or `[!benchmark]` tags for tests that shouldn't run by default
3. **Tag hierarchy**: Use consistent tagging scheme across the project
4. **File naming**: Follow `test_<feature>.cpp` pattern

#### CI/CD Integration
```bash
# Essential CI test command
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter junit::out=results.xml

# For coverage analysis
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter console --success

# For performance tracking
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --durations yes
```

This comprehensive guide ensures robust, maintainable, and efficient testing practices for OrcaSlicer development with Claude Code, incorporating all critical knowledge from the official Catch2 documentation.
